notes: Processing times are sourced from Home Affairs published medians and 90th percentiles as reported in mid-2025 to mid-2026. Home Affairs updates these monthly; figures here reflect what migration-advisory sites have most recently quoted from the official tool.

Planning levels are the permanent Migration Program annual caps. Temporary visas (482, 417, 462, 485, 500) do not have annual caps in the permanent Migration Program; the annualCap field is omitted for them.
189 SkillSelect cutoff varies by occupation; the score recorded here is the LOWEST cutoff (trades) for the most recent round, with a note about the higher general baseline.
Home Affairs blocks automated fetches (HTTP 403), so processing-time figures were corroborated across multiple migration-advisor summaries that quote the official tool, rather than fetched directly.

189.name: Skilled Independent

recentCutoff.notes: 65 was the lowest cutoff (building trades). General/ICT occupations were invited at 85-110 points in the same round.

notes: Latest official round 13 November 2025 issued ~10,000 invitations.
An unofficial third round on 4 June 2026 (Round 3 figures crowdsourced pending official publication) also showed 65-100 point range.

190.name: Skilled Nominated
notes: Planning level of 33,000 may be reported as combined with 491 in some sources.
State nomination required; cutoff scores set per state, not by SkillSelect.

491.name: Skilled Work Regional (Provisional)
notes: Same processing time bracket reported for both Family-Sponsored and State/Territory-nominated streams.
Planning level may be reported combined with 190 in some sources.

482.name: Skills in Demand (formerly TSS)
notes: Temporary visa, no annual cap in the permanent Migration Program.
Replaced the Temporary Skill Shortage visa name in December 2024.
Streams: Core Skills (uses CSOL), Specialist Skills, Labour Agreement.

186.name: Employer Nomination Scheme
notes: Annual cap 44,000 is the total Employer Sponsored category, which includes 186 and 187 streams.
Processing time shown is for the Direct Entry stream; TRT stream is similar (~13 months p50).
Labour Agreement stream is much faster (~5 months p50).

417.name: Working Holiday
notes: Temporary visa, no annual cap in the permanent Migration Program.
Most applications decided within 24-48 hours of lodgement.

462.name: Work and Holiday
notes: Temporary visa, no annual cap in the permanent Migration Program.
Country-specific annual quotas apply but are managed separately from the permanent Migration Program.

485.name: Temporary Graduate
notes: Temporary visa, no annual cap in the permanent Migration Program.
Only median (50%) commonly published; 90th percentile not consistently reported in sources reviewed.

500.name: Student
notes: Temporary visa, no annual cap in the permanent Migration Program.
p90 quoted by sources reflects ~95th percentile in some Home Affairs tool snapshots; varies sharply by education sector and country.
